item.title: Agents need an identity, and your IT department will say no
item.description:
Abstract

Everyone agrees AI agents should be treated like employees: their own identity, scoped permissions, an owner, monitoring and offboarding. Then you try to do it.

The agent on your laptop runs as you, because your machine is the security context. Your IT team rejects the application identity you ask for, because it doesn’t do MFA. Half your backends never see Entra ID at all, because they authenticate with personal access tokens. And the moment an agent can act on behalf of a user, “who owns this agent” quietly turns into “whose permissions does it have”.

item.title: Letting AI operate production Azure — what it gets wrong
item.description:
Abstract

Real failure stories from AI-assisted operations, each with the guardrail that fixed it:

  • an Azure GET can’t prove a property is settable (recommended four times off an empty read);
  • advising a change from a stale read in the middle of a cutover;
  • restating a verified fact until it’s wrong;
  • a disk caching change that hot-detached a production disk;
  • “a freeze is not a control”.

Plus the patterns that worked: subagents, cross-model review with gh copilot, and grep-verifying every HIGH finding. It’s honest, funny, and very MVP.

item.title: Hitting Reset
item.description:
10 Years, It is hard to believe that I have been posting thoughts here that long. And how so much has changed since I begun?

I started this journey with the encouragement of some amazing people in Microsoft, as an opportunity to spread the news about Hyper-V and even more relevant at the time System Center Virtual Machine Manager which was still known by its code name!.
